newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Gloom grips Tokyo rubber after baht move.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Gloom grips Tokyo rubber after baht move.

text.p: The gloom in Japan's rubber futures markets is likely to increase next week as the news of the floating of the baht dealt another blow to the already bearish market, Japanese traders said on Friday.
"Amid the circumstances of no bullish factors in sight, the move added further gloom to the markets," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Overseas rubber prices will face downward pressure as a tumble in the baht makes it easier for shippers in Thailand to reduce prices, the traders said.
The Thai government announced on Wednesday that it would float its overvalued baht, which resulted in a 15-20 percent devaluation.
The analyst said that the benchmark December rubber futures contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange would probe the downside at 106.00 yen in the near-term.
The contract was quoted at 110.6 yen per kg at the start of trade on Friday, against Thursday's close of 112.3 yen.
Similarly, benchmark December on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was 111.0 yen at the opening, compared with 112.7 yen.
The traders said the bearish sentiment was likely to linger during the summer.
"The markets have not yet absorbed all the bearish factors," another analyst at a commodity broker said.
Another bearish factor was the expectation that rubber stocks in Japan would start climbing again from mid-July after decreasing in recent months.
A seasonal rise in rubber output in overseas markets and signs of poor-quality rubber coming into Japan's rubber futures markets were also seen as negative factors, the traders said.

Thai rubber to Japan was offered sharply lower at 95.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, down from 105.00 U.S. cents on June 27. The offer prices to Japan are seen slipping further in the near-term.

The only positive factor for the market was that open interest of rubber futures was showing signs of increasing slightly due to growing selling interest in the course of the recent rapid downward slide.
Open interest in rubber futures has been above 11,000 lots since June 30.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 122 yen per kg as of Friday, compared with 128 yen on June 27.
